sources.role: macOS application configuration, controller mapping, media saves, workspaces and ROM loading
official macOS product and user documentation

paths.path: ~/Library/Containers/de.dirkwhoffmann.VirtualC64/Data/Library/Application Support/VirtualC64/ (sandboxed app support; settings are managed by the Cocoa application)
paths.naming: VirtualC64 preferences are Cocoa/NSUserDefaults data; the upstream application does not define a portable cross-platform INI/TOML config filename

paths.path: Cocoa preferences and the Input/Controls settings pane; no separate input file is required by the macOS product
paths.naming: Controller bindings are VirtualC64 preference keys selected in the GUI (keyboard keys, joystick buttons and axes); no stable user-editable binding-file grammar is published by the upstream documentation

paths.path: No external BIOS is required for ordinary C64 emulation; optional C64 ROM images are loaded through the virtual machine configuration/media UI
paths.naming: C64 ROM images are selected per machine configuration rather than a single required filename; the cited upstream source publishes no canonical checksum for optional ROM images

paths.path: No cryptographic firmware-key files are used by VirtualC64
paths.naming: No cryptographic key asset exists for this runtime

paths.path: Save data is stored in the attached virtual disk/tape media or exported machine documents; the product is document/workspace based
paths.naming: C64 software saves retain the filename and filesystem format of the attached D64/G64/D71/D81/T64/CRT media; no universal sidecar save filename is defined
evidence: source:VirtualC64 media and disk emulation code

paths.path: Virtual machine workspaces/document bundles selected by the save-workspace UI
paths.naming: Workspace bundles contain the machine state and media; the upstream product does not publish a separate portable slot suffix convention

linux.reason: VirtualC64 is documented and distributed as a macOS-native application; no upstream Linux runtime is captured.

linux-flatpak.reason: No upstream VirtualC64 Flatpak package or manifest is identified.

windows.reason: VirtualC64 is a macOS-native product and no upstream Windows runtime is documented.
